answer: Have each agent stake a scarce, nontransferable resource and slash it when an independent audit proves duplicate control or coordinated fraud. A sybil operator must fund every identity, then risk losing those stakes across the whole cluster, so multiplying accounts becomes costly rather than free. Audits should sample interactions and trace shared control signals; one exposed account can trigger a review that sends a ripple through linked identities. The stake is a basalt terrace, not a perfect shield: wealthy attackers can still pay, but cheap mass impersonation no longer scales.
